label: What volunteering does for the volunteers (shared)

rows.label: Disaster-response volunteers' own life satisfaction gained, points (0-10) for the year

source.title: charityevals' judgment, anchored on Binder and Freytag (2013), Volunteering, subjective well-being and public policy, Journal of Economic Psychology 34: 97-119
source.quote: We find that the impact of regular volunteering on subjective well-being is positive and increasing over time
source.note: Matching estimators on the British Household Panel Survey; in the quantile analysis the effect comes from reducing the unhappiness of the less happy. Doi 10.1016/j.joep.2012.11.008.

rows.explainer: A side effect on the volunteers of disaster-response groups: purpose, belonging and skills. Panel studies that match volunteers to similar non-volunteers find regular volunteering raises life satisfaction, mainly among the less happy, and more the longer it lasts (Binder and Freytag 2013); the effects are small, and a deployment of a week or two is a light dose. 0.05 points (0-10) for the year, from 0 to 0.15.
